analysis:
The PR changes two call sites in MiMoV26NativeLoadTransaction.swift (head lines ~963-964 and ~1074). Each adds `onRefusal: self.budget.directChargeRefusalSignal()` to the MiMoV26ManagedMediaReservation constructor, which charges the process ledger when media is admitted. This only adds a callback on admission refusal. I saw nothing in the visible diff that changes ownership, rollback, retirement ordering, lock order, permit settlement, the native shutdown proof, or alias detachment. The rest of the supplied files (registry, transaction lifecycle, retire(), commitPublication, sealConstructionForPublication) are unchanged context. I traced the interactions: the reservation is stored in mediaReservations under the lock before any further veto, and the refusal path still calls disposeUnstartedEncodedPromise and removeSettledMediaReservation. Refusal signalling in the constructor happens before the reservation is created, so it cannot affect the retained-owner invariants.

Unverified contract: the implementation of `GlobalKVCacheBudget.directChargeRefusalSignal()` and the new `onRefusal` parameter in MiMoV26ManagedMediaReservation are outside the supplied evidence. I cannot tell whether the callback runs under ledger or transaction locks, whether it can reenter the registry or transaction, or whether it could affect admission accounting, or whether it exposes content. A reviewer of those files should check that the callback is nonblocking, carries no prompt, media or path data, and cannot be used by a consumer to trigger a refusal storm or a DoS. Relevant threat IDs: T-010 and T-029 for availability, and TB-007. T-041 is not affected, since no cache storage code changed. The transaction file itself contains no regression that I could identify.
